utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-95-14-R77.3-I, thank you, the Prosecutor versus Stjepan Seselj and Domagoj Margetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. First of all, I'd like to know whether the accused understand -- hear me in a language they understand. Could I ask you -- I don't know yet who is Mr. Margetic, who is Mr. Seselj. Perhaps the one to the left -- well, you first, please, could you tell me whether you hear me in a language you understand and who you are. THE ACCUSED SESELJ: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm Stjepan Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And from your answer, I take it that you do hear me in a language you understand? THE ACCUSED SESELJ: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj. Mr. Margetic, same questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please push the microphone. Yes. THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] I am Domagoj Margetic, and I do understand everything that's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then I'd like to have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, David Akerson on behalf of the OTP. To my right is Jason Dominguez. Case manager is Sebastian van Hooydonk, and your internal is with us as well, Pierre Taponier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am Zeljko Olujic, an attorney-at-law from Croatia, and I defend Stjepan Seselj, who is a writer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that you're crossed. Yes, Mr. Olujic. Thank you. And then Defence counsel for Mr. Margetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUMANCIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Zeljko Dumancic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question. Are you Defence counsel registered? Mr. Olujic, it's not the first time we meet each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUMANCIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have informed the registry and my registration is probably underway now. All my papers have arrived at the Tribunal, however I did appear before this Court in other cases but during the the pre-trial stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you are a member of the Association of Defence Counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUMANCIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have applied. All of it is underway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore it's not for sure that you'll be in a position to continue to defend Mr. Margetic, but we'll deal with that at a later stage. For the purposes of this hearing, I'll just ask you as Defence counsel. Let me first explain, especially to you, Mr. Margetic and Mr. Seselj, the purpose of this hearing. The purpose of this hearing is to verify whether you received, read, and have understood the charges brought against you and to hear from you what position you take in that respect, whether you plead guilty or not guilty. The consequences being that if you enter a plea of guilty, that no further hearings on evidence will take place but then a date will be set to hear any argument in respect of sentencing, whereas if you do plead not guilty, then the case will be heard in full. The Prosecution will present its case. You will be in a position to present the Defence case, and then finally verdict will be reached. And if that would be a guilty verdict, then sentence will be pronounced. That's just my explanation of the purpose of this hearing. I have by now verified that you're assisted by counsel. May I ask, first of all, counsel whether they've received a copy of the indictment. Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. My client, Stjepan Seselj, a writer, did receive the indictment. We studied it carefully and he is going to enter a plea here before you today. He is going to plead not guilty to all the charges in this indictment, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll deal with that later, Mr. Olujic. As a matter of fact, I asked whether you had received a copy of the indictment, but you gave already some of the answers I would have put to you next. Mr. Seselj, I would like to ask you whether you could confirm what is just said by counsel, that you have received and that you have understood, and that you have discussed the content of the indictment with counsel. THE ACCUSED SESELJ: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Then I would have the same questions for Mr. Margetic, and perhaps I now start with you, Mr. Margetic. Have you received a copy of the indictment? Have you read it? And have you understood it? THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] Yes, we've received the indictment. I have understood the indictment. Am I supposed to enter my plea now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I'll ask you at a later stage. THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] I understood the indictment, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you were in a position to discuss it with your counsel? THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] I don't know how much time I have to answer this question of yours. It would require a bit of an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the question seems quite simple, but if you say, I need a minute or two minutes to explain -- THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I have discussed the indictment with my lawyer, but I wanted to say that the Government of Croatia gave me the indictment under strange circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll hear then, if you consider this then to be relevant, then we'll hear about that at a later stage because at the end of this hearing I'll ask you if there's any procedural issue you would like to raise at that moment. Then for you, Mr. Dumancic, you can confirm that you have discussed the content of the indictment with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUMANCIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. We have understood the indictment and we have elaborated on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you, Mr. Dumancic. Would you prefer to have the whole indictment to be read out to you? We'll then do that. If you say we have sufficiently studied it, so it would be sufficient at a later stage to put the counts to you on which you're supposed to enter a plea, then please tell me. Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have understood your question. We, as Defence counsel, believe that there is no need to have the indictment read out. We have read it. We have understood it. So we are waiving our right to have it read out today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dumancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUMANCIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An identical answer, we also do not consider it necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dumancic. Then you, Mr. Seselj and Mr. Margetic, you will be called to enter a plea within 30 days of this initial appearance. But you are allowed to enter a plea right on this very moment. So if you think you would need more time to think it over, you've got 30 days for that. If you say, I would like to enter a plea today, then we'll further proceed. Could I hear from you whether you want to enter a plea today or whether you would like to delay entering a plea. THE ACCUSED SESELJ: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'll put the counts to you at a later stage, but I do understand that you want to enter a plea today and not at a later stage. Yes. Mr. Margetic. THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] I do wish to enter my plea today, Your Honour, I do not -- I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll read the counts of the indictment to you and then ask you to enter a plea. I'll start with you, Mr. Seselj. You are charged under Count 2 with contempt of the Tribunal punishable under the Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(ii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED SESELJ: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Trial Chamber records the plea of not guilty on Count 1 on your behalf. Please be seated. Mr. Margetic, you've been charged with two counts, to just put it short to you, the first one deals with the disclosure of the identity of a protected witness, the disclosure of extracts of a closed session testimony, and disclosing the facts that a protected witness had testified in non-public proceedings. That's the first count. And the second deals with that you continued publishing it even when you were ordered to stop that. I'll first read the first count brought against you, that is Count 1, and that's about the disclosure of the testimony and the identity of the witness. Count 1, contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under the Tribunal's inherent powers and Rule 77(A)(ii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. How do you plead to Count 1, guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Trial Chamber or I as a Judge on behalf of the Trial Chamber records the plea of not guilty on Count 1. And on Count 2, Mr. Margetic, which I'll read to you, that's also contempt of the Tribunal punishable under the Tribunal's inherent power and Rule 77(A)(ii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal here being interference with the administration of justice by disclosing the identity of protected witness, the extracts of closed session testimony, and the facts that a protected witness testified in a non-public proceedings. How do you plead to Count 2, guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED MARGETIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then your plea of not guilty on Count 2 is put on the record. You may be seated. There is no need to discuss any detention issue, since the Office of the Prosecutor has not applied for a warrant of arrest, but rather for summons. I take it that this does not change?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any other issues you'd like to raise at this moment? It's not the ordinary way we proceed here because usually accused are in the United Nations Detention Unit. That could mean that organising disclosure, et cetera, is a bit different from usual. But is there any issue you would like to raise, Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are going to provide the supporting materials today to Defence counsel. I anticipate that there will be very little additional disclosure. I anticipate that this trial could be in -- this case could be in trial posture in a short period of time, at least from the Prosecution's perspective. And I think it's beneficial that because this is a contempt case, it takes place in as close proximity to the event, in keeping with normal contempt cases. So we would ask the Court to try to put the case on a fast track in order to expedite the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that you're disclosing the supporting material today. Would that be on a confidential basis? Would there be any need for an order, because the whole subject of this case is of course such that if this material would not be disclosed confidentially, then finally the whole issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is -- if these were public documents, then the OTP would do, as a matter of fact, what it blames the accused to have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: The disclosure to the Defence and the receipt, actually, has a disclaimer that they are not to disclose. It is confidential. But I would not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it usual that there is an order by the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I don't have any problem with you issuing an order. I think that's an excellent idea in addition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nothing more from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Nothing more from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the Defence, Mr. Olujic, on behalf of Mr. Seselj. Any issue to be raised at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point in time, as far as I can hear, my learned friend has documentation available. Regrettably, I could not infer from what he said that we would be receiving it as early as possible. The second thing I have to say, especially in relation to what you said in your introductory remarks, Your Honour, this is a bit of an unusual point but I have to say it nevertheless. When the indictment was issued against writer Stjepan Seselj, we were summoned by an investigator of the Hague Tribunal of the 17th this month for an interview. Now, if we do not get the relevant material, I'm just mentioning this in passing, could the Prosecutor please take upon himself to submit to us as early as possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you for one second. Mr. Akerson, I did hear you say that you would disclose today all the supporting materials. So there seems to be some misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct, Your Honour. We're going to turn it over after this hearing's over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll receive it today, Mr. Olujic, so that issue seems then to be clarified. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then there's nothing else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Olujic. Mr. Dumancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUMANCIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after we receive the relevant material, after we have a look at it in its entirety, it is only then that we will be in a position to notify you of the time that we may need for preparing our defence. Before that, unfortunately the Defence could not really say how much time it requires to do everything that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand scheduling is something to come once you've seen the material. Supporting material is not very extensive from what I understood Mr. Akerson. If there's nothing else, I noted that there was an issue about strange circumstances under which the indictment was delivered to one of the accused. Is there anything that should be said about that or would you like to consult with your clients first? It was raised earlier and then I said we'll come to it at a later stage, if need be, but if no one wants to raise the issue of these strange circumstances under which the indictment was handed out then I leave it to that. Then there's nothing more on the agenda. We'll adjourn. No date will yet be set for the next hearing. The Senior Legal Officer will keep in touch with the parties to see whether disclosure is complete and to ask for any further information in respect of scheduling that the Chamber might need before finally scheduling the date for trial. We adjourn.
